title: BitPattern: Enabling Efficient Bit-Serial Acceleration of Deep Neural Networks through Bit-Pattern Pruning
problem: Bit-serial DNN accelerators struggle with unstructured bit sparsity, causing workload imbalance and inefficient memory access due to irregular non-zero bit distributions.
motivation: Bit-serial computation exploits sparsity but requires structured patterns for efficient hardware implementation; unstructured sparsity defeats hardware optimizations.
method: Algorithm-hardware co-design: (1) algorithm level identifies optimal bit-pattern combinations via pruning, applies compression encoding for weight storage, merges similar patterns for workload balancing; (2) hardware implements bit-serial accelerator with dedicated pattern decoder and PE exploiting structured bit-pattern sparsity. Pattern-based approach vs bit-level irregularity.
key_novelty: Structured bit-pattern pruning to convert unstructured bit sparsity into hardware-friendly regular patterns.
contributions: Bit-pattern pruning algorithm with pattern-similarity-based workload merging
Compression encoding reducing weight storage by 1.72x
Co-designed bit-serial accelerator with pattern decoder achieving 2.11x speedup and 1.86x energy saving vs SOTA
limitations: Evaluation on deep learning benchmarks; specifics (model sizes, datasets) not detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: Pattern-based bit sparsity for bit-serial accelerators
